notes:
Inbound self-serve signup converted to trial last week. Customer complaint is latency variability and some aborted calls from browser widget. Key excerpts from discovery call:
- Customer: "chat replies sometimes take 1s-1.5s from EU users; causes perceived slowness in our live chat UI"
- AE notes: 'using default endpoint, likely us-west region; client-side timeout set to 10s, but UI aborts after 2.5s for perceived slow responses'
- SE (Carlos): recommended quick wins during call: pick region closest to majority of users (eu-west-1 for EU, us-east-1 for NA), enable streaming responses in widget, trim system prompt + reduce top_p to speed decoding, set client timeout to 30s for long responses and show streaming spinner at 200ms, paginate history to reduce token length per request.
Performance specifics they shared (from local timing): avg response token time ~60ms/token in us-west-2 tests; p95 spikes to ~450ms total for 350-token responses. They run chat and summarization workloads; throughput low (5-15 reqs/min) but strict latency expectation for live chat (<300ms render to first token).
Security/context: SMB; willing to use hosted API but need SOC2 doc and SSO for admin console. No on-prem requirement. Data residency preference: US for PII customers.
AE/SE commitment: SE will provide a sample region-config and prompt-trim checklist, plus a small perf harness script (node/python) for them to run against us-east-1 vs us-west-2 vs eu-west-1. Also offered to enable short-term increased burst credits on trial account to remove capacity as a blocker.
Customer quote: "If we can get consistent first-token under 250ms we'll push to paid this quarter."
